newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem calls Cavallo hoodwinking remark "impolite".
newsitem.headline: Menem calls Cavallo hoodwinking remark "impolite".

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem Saturday called his former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo "impolite" for having urged him to admit he was "hoodwinked" on a huge smuggling syndicate in the Customs Service.

"Former minister Cavallo is somewhat wrong," Menem told journalists in his native province of La Rioja, 700 miles northwest of Buenos Aires. "...when he says the president was hoodwinked, he is being impolite."

Campaigning against corruption, Cavallo said in an interview published Friday in La Nacion newspaper: "I hope Menem has the courage to admit that he has been hoodwinked. He has the opportunity to throw out those who deceived him and start a real fight against corruption."

Cavallo, who was fired in July after guiding Argentina to economic stability and zero inflation, said charges of a $10 billion smuggling ring and the arrest of one of his trusted former aides was a smokescreen to protect real criminals.
His replacement Roque Fernandez also rebuked Cavallo.
"To say that is not to know the President, it is a ridiculous assertion, and rather a lack of respect," he said.
Since he was dismissed, Cavallo has been engaged in a fierce battle with ministers and judges whom he accuses of protecting a corruption ring.
